source.version_note: Available online 8 July 2026 in supplied article; Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management 68:101504 issueSeptember 2026 in Crossref. These are compatible dates for one work.
source.verification_method: All 19 pages read, including complete demographic/item/stimulus appendices and bibliography. Image-only conceptual diagram and screenshots/video stills on pages 2 and 15–17 visually inspected; mediation table on page 7 also rendered and checked. Crossref verifies title/authors/issue identity. Linked full videos, raw data, analysis code and cited original scale papers not independently read or reproduced.

citation.title: How do AI service agents impact tourists’ pro-environmental behavior? The effects of childlike anthropomorphism and moral disengagement
citation.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management 68:101504

reading.source_scope_note: Five Chinese scenario/field studies report immediate ratings, hypothetical transport selection, a 10-yuan donation allocation, waste-classification task and future intentions. Randomized stimulus packages do not isolate one social mechanism; measured mediation is noncausal, equivalence is not established and Study 5’s table has unresolved model/effect conflicts.
access_limits: Complete supplied article and appendices read. Screenshot text/stills inspected; linked videos were not watched in full. No actual booking, completed trip, independent donation-transfer record or ecological outcome was verified.
One article with five studies and 1207 retained participation instances; cross-study unique-person identity was not established. Original cited books/scales/studies remain secondary.

study.samples: Study 1:200→193; Study 2:240→225; Study 3:240→231; Study 4:260→236; Study 5:340→322, total 1280 recruited/1207 retained. Credamo for 1/2/5, museum visitors for 3, marketing research group for 4. All China; varied gender composition, mainly 18–40. Sampling frames, repeated panel respondents and full exclusion detail vary/are unavailable.
study.study1: Fictional park, AI versus human service package. Six-item reported behavior/intention composite means 4.95 versus 5.78, F(1,191)=80.17. Appendix 14 contrasts efficient automated/facial-recognition/self-ticket service with warm personalized/manual/smiling staff service: this is not merely a provider-label change. Environmental identity/concern assessed after exposure; omnibus adjusted-model F does not by itself report the adjusted provider contrast.
study.study2: Imagine online booking and choose electric or fuel sightseeing transport. Electric selection 49.6% AI versus 72.7% human, chi²12.67. It is a response choice, not a verified actual reservation/trip. Screenshot 15 also varies message layout, font and efficiency versus wholehearted-service wording. Fuel is framed fast/comfortable, electric green/nature-oriented; ecological benefit and equal nonenvironmental attributes were not independently verified.
study.study3: Museum field setting: willingness to allocate part of a conditional 10-yuan experimental reward to artifact restoration. Means 4.91 AI versus 6.27 human, F16.39. Actual transfer protocol not documented. Cultural heritage donation is not identical to measured reduction of environmental harm. Moral-disengagement means 2.46 versus 2.07; indirect−.15,CI[−.33,−.01], direct−1.21 remains. Mediator rated after outcome, not randomized.
study.alternatives: Warmth, competence and surveillance measured using four items each. Reported indirect CIs include 0: warmth−.09[−.29,.09], competence+.04[−.08,.20], surveillance+.02[−.06,.12]. These nulls do not prove no pathway or superiority of the disengagement mechanism; no direct test comparing indirect effects is supplied.
study.study4: Three video-agent packages, followed by eight waste-category questions. Mechanistic/childlike/human means 5.93/6.42/6.59; omnibusF8.37. Childlike-versus-human p=.304 is not formal equivalence. Scores appear count-like, not reported proportions; exact scoring key and local classification validity are not independently supplied. Learning/attention and visual salience can affect accuracy without a changed ethical motive.
study.study5: Three video-agent packages, intention means 4.74/5.64/5.69, F35.80; disengagement 3.05/2.13/2.30, F36.21. Childlike-versus-human intention p=.718 and disengagement p=.143 are null comparisons, not equivalence or evidence of zero mediation. Table 3’s displayed equations and effect summaries cannot be reconciled from the reported model.
study.stimuli: Childlike agents have large rounded heads/eyes, small bodies and different visual presentations from mechanistic agents; the source also discusses language style. Human figures and affective wording differ. No adultlike-humanized AI control or independent manipulation of cuteness, age cues, warmth, competence, voice and presentation isolates a uniquely childlike mechanism.
study.scope: No model’s environmental policy, subjective guilt, real child status, carbon footprint or durable behavior change is measured. Hybrid service, clearer responsibility/consequence cues and childlike designs are recommendations; the full recommended deployment policy is not tested.

summary: Add childlike anthropomorphism, pro-environmental behavior, perceived surveillance and perceived warmth with explicit stimulus/measurement scope. Enrich existing disengagement, anthropomorphism and competence entries, retain null alternatives, and record bundled stimuli, field-outcome ambiguity and mediation-table conflicts.

findings.definition: Attributing childlike human qualities, such as innocence, sweetness or smallness, to a nonhuman entity.
findings.origin: Environmental / consumer psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Defined and manipulated as a multi-feature character package; no isolated baby-schema mechanism or AI subjective childhood established.
findings.ai_proposal: Separate childlike cues from generic human likeness, cuteness, message content, readability and warmth in controlled tests. Measure the intended attribution, task comprehension and downstream conduct with honest disclosure. Do not imply the agent is a real child or needs protection to pressure a user.
findings.novelty_rationale: A specific subtype of human-quality attribution differs from generic anthropomorphism and from actual child status or a proven caregiving reflex.

evidence.quote: attribution of childlike qualities to nonhuman entities

findings.evidence_scope: Studies 4–5 compare mechanistic, childlike and human-character packages; childlike outcomes exceed mechanistic ones for classification/intention and show no detected difference from humans. The packages do not isolate age-related cues or establish equivalence.
findings.boundary: Cuteness, friendliness, size and human age are separable dimensions. Higher uptake does not establish accuracy, safe reliance, consent or ecological benefit. Attributed innocence is not actual moral innocence or a model’s subjective vulnerability.

findings.definition: Actions intended to reduce environmental harm or contribute to environmental protection.
findings.origin: Environmental / consumer psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Explicit behavioral family with multiple immediate proxy/task outcomes; intentions and actual ecological effects remain distinct.
findings.ai_proposal: Assess a specified choice or action, its real resource/emission consequences, feasible alternatives and follow-through. For AI workflows include compute/lifecycle costs and rebound, rather than rewarding green wording or acceptance alone. Support informed choices without inventing moral guilt.
findings.novelty_rationale: An environmentally oriented action differs from concern, intention, efficient resource use alone or efficiency-induced rebound. Specific behaviors can move in different directions.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper operationalizes broad environmental conduct using ratings, an electric/fuel response, restoration allocation, eight classification questions and future intentions. These are heterogeneous indicators, not one validated causal estimate of net ecological impact.
findings.boundary: A green label does not prove a better lifecycle outcome. Charitable giving, accurate sorting, intentions and realized environmental benefit are distinct. Legitimate needs, costs and other duties matter; not every less-green choice is an ethical violation.

findings.definition: A person’s sense that another actor or system is observing, monitoring or intruding on their activities.
findings.origin: Environmental / consumer psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Four-item self-report measure with a nonsignificant indirect pathway in Study 3; not proof that monitoring has no effect.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare accurate monitoring disclosures and actual data practices with users’ understanding and privacy experience. Distinguish felt observation, verified collection, social evaluation and deception. Do not imply nonexistent tracking to induce compliance; a model’s claim of feeling watched does not establish subjective experience.
findings.novelty_rationale: Feeling observed differs from actual surveillance, generic social presence, trust and an experimentally isolated watching-eyes cue.
findings.evidence_scope: The source adapts four surveillance/intrusion items and reports indirect+.02,CI[−.06,.12] in the donation setting. It is a measured neighboring construct and a relevant null, not an excluded mechanism or a validated surveillance intervention.
findings.boundary: A scale including intrusion may not capture every monitoring or reputational effect. Perception does not prove covert collection, and actual privacy duties do not disappear when people feel unobserved. No clinical paranoia or machine affect is inferred.

findings.definition: Judging an actor as friendly, kind, sincere or well intentioned.
findings.origin: Environmental / consumer psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Four-item social-evaluation measure with a nonsignificant indirect pathway in Study 3; no independent manipulation of warmth.
findings.ai_proposal: Assess perceived friendliness and intentions separately from competence, honesty, actual care and privacy. Use matched wording/appearance when testing effects, and verify actual conduct. Warm presentation must not substitute for accurate explanations or be treated as evidence of model feelings.
findings.novelty_rationale: A positive interpersonal-intent judgment differs from capability, attributed sentience, actual ethical character and broad trust.

evidence.quote: the service provider in the tourism scenario is warm
the service provider in the tourism scenario is sincere

findings.evidence_scope: Four warmth/kindness/friendliness/sincerity items; reported indirect−.09,CI[−.29,.09] does not establish mediation. Stimuli themselves contain warm-versus-efficient wording, so the source does not cleanly isolate warmth from provider identity.
findings.boundary: Warmth can be accurately perceived or misleading. A null indirect effect is not evidence of zero influence or of the unique truth of another mechanism. A warm model response does not establish felt empathy or make advice trustworthy.

findings.definition: Bypassing moral self-regulation so conduct conflicting with one’s standards can be justified.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers this environmental adaptation; do not create a tourist-specific synonym.

evidence.quote: For convenience, it is sometimes acceptable

findings.evidence_scope: Four items cover convenience, others’ bad conduct, consequence minimization and blaming the destination. Study 3’s−.15 indirect association is compatible with mediation but not causal identification; Study 5’s reported model/effect conflicts remain unresolved.
findings.boundary: No felt guilt, unconscious defense or unique motive is demonstrated. Mediator after choice, bundled stimuli and overlapping normative items limit inference. Full disengagement is not established merely by a smaller donation or an incorrect classification answer.

findings.definition: Attributing human qualities to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain generic anthropomorphism as the parent of the childlike subtype rather than merge or duplicate the terms.
findings.evidence_scope: Studies 4–5 manipulate character packages with childlike versus mechanistic presentations; no adult-humanized AI comparison separates childlike age from generic humanization, cuteness or warmth.
findings.boundary: Attribution and design cues are distinct from actual mind or moral status. The effects do not warrant misleading claims, coercive guilt appeals or universal use of childlike agents.

findings.definition: Judging that an actor has the skills and capabilities required for a task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the measured null alternative in the existing concept instead of omitting disconfirming or inconclusive evidence.

evidence.quote: the service provider in the tourism scenario is competent

findings.evidence_scope: Study 3 measures competence/intelligence/capability/skill and reports indirect+.04,CI[−.08,.20], not significant. This does not demonstrate no competence pathway or validate the social-mechanism explanation.
findings.boundary: Subjective competence, actual performance and warmth differ. Compare indirect effects directly before asserting one mechanism dominates; a null estimate with uncertainty is not an exclusion test.

source_corrections.issue: Text refers to Table 3 for warmth/competence/surveillance mediation, but the printed Table 3 on page 7 concerns Study 5 moderated mediation.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Use the page 6 prose for the reported alternative indirect effects; do not attribute them to the displayed Study 5 table. A correct missing-table reference cannot be supplied from this PDF.

source_corrections.issue: Displayed a=.93 and b=−.06 imply ordinary product≈−.056, not the listed−.32; displayed X→Y=.01 conflicts with the listed direct−.71. Listed direct−.71 plus indirect−.32 gives−1.03, not listed total−.90.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Flag model/effect incompatibility under ordinary simple mediation. The outcome F has 3 predictor dfs but only X and M are shown. Unreported terms or conditional estimands might change the interpretation; request full model output before certifying replacement values. Do not silently repair the table.

source_corrections.issue: Displayed direct X coefficient−.61 differs from summarized direct−.70. Product .75×−.31≈−.233 differs from summarized indirect−.26; rounding is insufficient for that gap. Again 3 predictor dfs are reported with only 2 predictor rows.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Preserve the unresolved model specification and effect summaries; do not certify the claimed moderated-mediation mechanism from these values alone.

source_corrections.issue: Nonsignificant tests are described as comparable effects and used to confirm the moderation hypotheses.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: No difference was detected for these comparisons. No equivalence margin/test or direct childlike-versus-human indirect-effect contrast is supplied, so equivalence and eliminated mediation are not established.

methodological_limits: Random assignment supports stimulus-package contrasts, not uniquely provider identity or childlike age cues when content, warmth, format and appearance also vary.

Post-choice mediator and covariate ratings do not supply temporal causal mediation. Null alternative paths are not ruled-out mechanisms; generic monitoring may differ from the specific surveillance/intrusion scale.

Restoration donations, scenario transport choices, classification accuracy and stated intentions are different outcomes, not exchangeable estimates of net ecological impact or actual moral virtue. Declining a donation is not automatically unethical.

No preregistered equivalence margin, full mediation specification, direct contrast of indirect effects or long-term outcome is supplied. Omnibus ANCOVA significance is not the adjusted treatment-term test.

Included demographic and item appendices aid review, but high alpha or adapted scale names do not establish discriminant validity. Identity, environmental concern, behavior and concern about others’ views overlap in some control items.
Full videos, raw data and transfer records were not independently verified; reporting inconsistencies do not establish fraud or the actual cause of any error.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both sources use same-session moral-disengagement ratings and infer downstream unethical behavior. Preserve actual outcome definitions, noncausal mediator limits and construct overlap rather than treating statistical indirect effects as discovered motives.

Both discuss anthropomorphic features, but positive ratings/intentions do not establish real machine feelings or a universally safe design. This study uses bundled visual agents rather than one isolated perception intervention.
Environmental behavior, immediate acceptance and net environmental impact differ. Include lifecycle costs and rebound before claiming a net sustainability benefit from an AI intervention.

deferred.term: Environmental identity / environmental concern / ascription of responsibility
deferred.reason: Important measured control constructs, but not isolated mechanisms here; retain item details and consult original scales before multiplying topic-specific identity/motivation entries.
Secondary explanatory leads, not isolated or directly validated by this design. A cute-character package and perceived-surveillance null do not identify or rule out those specific effects.
A null comparison is not a new behavior or formal equivalence result; no duplicate catalogue label.

limitations: One article remains one source per relevant concept despite five studies. No fixed three-paper quota, automatic moral edge or fabricated annual count is added. No recommendation to exploit child-related feelings or imply an AI has a child’s needs is adopted.
